symptom: A PIT evidence callback may return an invalid status, negative count or non-finite count while the lifecycle still proceeds to DRY_RUN_OK or PASS if the three violation counts do not compare greater than zero.
lesson: PIT evidence is a runtime trust boundary, not a TypeScript guarantee. Relational comparisons against zero do not reject NaN, negative or missing counters, and do not validate status or NOT_APPLICABLE reason.
guardrail: Before reporting DRY_RUN_OK or PASS, require PASS/NOT_APPLICABLE status, non-empty validator identity/version, nonnegative safe-integer counts and an explicit NOT_APPLICABLE reason. Preserve existing positive-violation rejection and never infer research readiness.
